messages:
maria: Heads-up: ingest cost for metrics from mobile proxies spiked again yesterday, ~2.4x baseline. Seems correlated with a new sampling rollout on canary.

sam: ugh. which sampling rollout? the reservoir one we tested last week?

maria: yeah, that one. canary group kept full enrichment on, but edge sampler dropped ~80% of points. our billing shows the remaining 20% carrying a lot more enrich work per metric (kv lookups + joiners).

ayush: quick summary of what happened from the sampler side: we used reservoir sampling keyed by device_id, rate 0.2, but the client attach_attrs flag got flipped so frontend sent full attrs for sampled keys only. that means the pipeline did late enrich for those and hit lots of lookups.

diane: so we saved token volume but increased enrichment cardinality and lookups -> net cost up. tradeoff mismatch.

maria: exact. two proposals to debate:
- keep sampling at edge but attach lightweight keys only, do heavy enrich downstream in bulk (but amortizes lookups)
- or perform enrichment at the edge for sampled points and drop the rest (simpler attribution but pushes compute to edge)

sam: both have pros. edge-enrich makes downstream simpler and reduces routing, but it moves vendor/KMS calls outwards and complicates private deployment security.

ayush: also: deterministic hash sampling (by tenant/request_id) vs reservoir per-window. Deterministic makes attribution stable across retries and dedupe, which helps cost accounting.

diane: for cost attribution we need stable keys. If we do late enrichment, we must preserve a fingerprint (pref_key) so chargeback can reconstitute which tenant/feature consumed the cost.

maria: implementation draft for a middle-ground: sample at edge using deterministic hash, forward a compact envelope with precomputed minimal keyset (tenant_id, request_id, pref_key) and a flag enrich_prefetch:false. downstream enrichment service runs a batch enricher that accepts batched pref_keys and returns attributes via a streaming join.

sam: that sounds reasonable. can we avoid the per-sample synchronous lookups? need batch join window and watermarking.

ayush: proposed config snippet for the sampler:

```yaml
sampling:
  mode: deterministic
  key: request_id
  rate: 0.1
  forward_attrs: ["tenant_id","request_id","pref_key"]
  attach_attrs: false
```

maria: batch join config idea:

```yaml
enricher:
  mode: streaming-batch
  max_batch_ms: 250
  max_batch_items: 1000
  dedupe_on: pref_key
  fallback: async-queue
```

diane: what about failure modes? if the enricher lags, do we keep the minimal envelope and mark as un-enriched or block ingestion (backpressure)?

sam: we should avoid blocking producers. plan: mark as un-enriched with a trace flag and schedule backfill; downstream cost reports should be able to reconcile once backfill completes.

ayush: reconciliation requires idempotent joins and a way to patch historical records. we have two options: (1) mutate stored metric envelopes with enriched attrs (hard) or (2) emit a reconciliation event that the billing system can join to correct attribution in aggregated rollups.

diane: lean to (2). less invasive and aligns with our cost-aggregation queries.

maria: rollout checklist I propose:
1) implement deterministic sampler and compact envelope schema v1 (add pref_key). 2) shipping batch enricher + reconciliation event schema. 3) canary 1% tenant group with attribution monitor dashboard. 4) expand with metered guardrails.

sam: + add an A/B to compare net cost per-tenant for edge-enrich vs late-batch for a matched cohort.

observability-bot: Note: scheduled job 'enrich-backfill' triggered 2026-03-22T08:40:12Z for canary cohort 1

maria: thanks bot. next steps: ayush and sam to prototype sampler+enricher this sprint. diane to spec reconciliation event shape and cost-correct queries. I'll put the canary run on the calendar and add a dashboard template. anything else?

diane: add an audit log requirement for downstream private deploys (KMS/HSM calls must remain server-side), otherwise edge-enrich becomes non-starter for some customers.

ayush: noted. will add a capability flag so deployment config can choose enrich_location: edge|batch with default batch.

sam: cool. I'll draft the RFC follow-up doc with config examples and perf/finance acceptance criteria.

maria: perfect — thanks all. I'll post a short summary in #product as well so PMs see the plan.
